sections.history: Karpaganatharkulam, whose Tevaram name is Tirukkadikkulam, lies near Thiruthuraipoondi (about 18 km) in the southern reaches of Tiruvarur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later; the lord here is called Karpaganathar, and the place name joins him to the celestial wish-granting tree.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian temple of the lower delta, the shrine enshrines Karpaganathar in the sanctum, worshipped in a rare hexagonal lingam, with the goddess Soundara Nayaki — also called Balasundari — in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The hexagonal form of the mula-lingam is a distinctive feature of this shrine.
sections.legends: The name Karpaganathar evokes the karpaga (kalpaka) tree of the gods, which grants every wish, so the lord is worshipped here as the giver of boons, who fulfils the prayers of his devotees as the celestial tree fulfils every desire. The goddess Soundara Nayaki, 'the beautiful lady,' also called Balasundari, stands beside him. As with many smaller delta shrines, the fuller sthala purana is preserved in local tradition and Sambandar's verses.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a village shrine. Pilgrims on the Paadal Petra trail of the southern delta include Karpaganatharkulam among their stops.
sections.experience: At Karpaganatharkulam the pilgrim comes to a wish-granting shrine, where the lord bears the name of the celestial tree. Before Karpaganathar in his rare hexagonal lingam and the beautiful Soundara Nayaki, the visitor brings the longings of the heart to a quiet Tevaram temple of the southern Kaveri country.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Karpaganatharkulam is about 18 km from Thiruthuraipoondi (via Thondiakadu, PIN 614703), in the southern reaches of Tiruvarur district, roughly 29 km from Vedaranyam. Thiruthuraipoondi is the nearest rail head, with buses and taxis to the village.
